::: {.result}
**Question.** What do we hear in a single note?

**Answer.** Four things: its pitch, loudness, timbre and duration. Each can change while the other three stay the same.
:::

## The four aspects {#four}

- **Pitch**: how high or low the note sounds.[^pitch]
- **Loudness**: how strong it sounds.
- **Duration**: how long it lasts.
- **Timbre** (say "TAM-ber"): what still tells two notes apart when their pitch, loudness and duration are the same. It is why a flute and a violin playing the same note, equally loud and equally long, still sound different.[^timbre]

All four are perceptions, measured by asking listeners.[^aspects]

## Hear each one change {#hear}


Each control changes one thing in the sound and leaves the rest fixed. To the ear the four aspects are nearly, not perfectly, independent: at the same power a low note sounds a little quieter than a middle one,[^iso] and the bright note a little louder than the pure one.[^spread]

## Two questions {#questions}

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
  <p class="wyla"><b>Try it:</b> six instruments, each playing middle C (lowest frequency 262 Hz) at about the same strength.</p>
  <div class="controls" id="fam"></div>
  <p class="cap">Each sound is a model built from pure tones, as the next page explains. The flute also has the breath noise and the slow wobble in pitch (vibrato) that a real flute has; none has the sound of a bow or a stick.</p>
</div>
</div>
```

**Question 1. Why does the piano have a pitch you can hum, while the drum gives a thud?** Not every drum lacks a pitch: a kettledrum has one.[^timp] The series explains that too.

**Question 2. Why do the instruments sound so different, even at the same pitch and loudness?**

::: {.result}
**Takeaway.** We hear four things in a note: pitch, loudness, timbre and duration, and each can change while the others stay the same. What in the sound sets each one is the next page.
:::

[^pitch]: The Acoustical Society of America defines pitch as the attribute by which sounds are ordered from low to high; it is measured as the frequency of the pure tone that listeners judge equally high. [Standard terminology: pitch](https://asastandards.org/terms/pitch/), 11.01; B. C. J. Moore, [*An Introduction to the Psychology of Hearing*](https://auditory.org/postings/2012/87.html), 6th ed., Emerald, 2012, chapter 6.
[^timbre]: Adapted from the ANSI/ASA definition of timbre (terminology 12.09), as quoted by Wikipedia, [Timbre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbre).
[^aspects]: Moore, [*An Introduction to the Psychology of Hearing*](https://auditory.org/postings/2012/87.html), 6th ed., 2012, chapters 4, 6 and 8 (loudness, pitch, timbre); R. Plomp, [*Aspects of Tone Sensation: A Psychophysical Study*](https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000212840), Academic Press, 1976.
[^iso]: ISO 226:2023, [*Acoustics — Normal equal-loudness-level contours*](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html); HyperPhysics, [Equal loudness curves](https://hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Sound/eqloud.html).
[^spread]: At the same power, sound spread over a wide range of frequencies is louder than sound bunched together: E. Zwicker, G. Flottorp and S. S. Stevens, ["Critical band width in loudness summation"](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.1908963), *J. Acoust. Soc. Am.* 29 (1957), 548–557.
[^timp]: HyperPhysics, [The Timpani](https://hyperphysics.gsu.edu/hbase/Music/timpani.html), tabulating A. H. Benade, [*Fundamentals of Musical Acoustics*](https://archive.org/details/fundamentalsofmu0000bena), Oxford University Press, 1976.

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, M = C.models, SR = 44100;
  // Sample peaks stay at or below 0.55: core.js sends sound through a gain of 0.55 and a compressor with threshold -10 dB,
  // and 0.55 * 0.55 = 0.30 is below it, so relative levels are exact.
  var PEAK = 0.55;

  // parts: [{f, amp, tau}] (tau 0 = steady). attack, release: raised-cosine ramps in seconds.
  function synth(parts, dur, attack, release) {
    var N = Math.floor(dur * SR), d = new Float32Array(N);
    parts.forEach(function (p) {
      if (p.f > SR / 2.3 || p.f <= 0 || !p.amp) return;
      var w = 2 * Math.PI * p.f / SR, c = Math.cos(w), s = Math.sin(w), re = 1, im = 0, e = p.amp;
      var dec = p.tau ? Math.exp(-1 / (p.tau * SR)) : 1, n1 = p.tau ? Math.min(N, Math.ceil(p.tau * SR * 9)) : N;
      for (var n = 0; n < n1; n++) { d[n] += e * im; var nr = re * c - im * s; im = re * s + im * c; re = nr; e *= dec; }
    });
    var a = Math.max(1, Math.floor(attack * SR)), r = Math.max(1, Math.floor(release * SR));
    for (var n = 0; n < a && n < N; n++) d[n] *= 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * n / a);
    for (var m = 0; m < r && m < N; m++) d[N - 1 - m] *= 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * m / r);
    return d;
  }
  function peakOf(d) { var p = 0; for (var i = 0; i < d.length; i++) p = Math.max(p, Math.abs(d[i])); return p; }
  function rmsOf(d, t0, t1) { var i0 = Math.floor(t0 * SR), i1 = Math.min(d.length, Math.floor(t1 * SR)), s = 0; for (var i = i0; i < i1; i++) s += d[i] * d[i]; return Math.sqrt(s / Math.max(1, i1 - i0)); }
  var cur = null;
  function play(d) {
    var a = C.ac(), t = a.currentTime;
    if (cur) { cur.g.gain.setTargetAtTime(0, t, 0.006); cur.src.stop(t + 0.06); cur = null; }
    var b = a.createBuffer(1, d.length, SR); b.getChannelData(0).set(d);
    var src = a.createBufferSource(), g = a.createGain(); src.buffer = b; src.connect(g); g.connect(C.out); src.start();
    cur = { src: src, g: g };
  }

  // ---- one note, four controls ----
  // Each timbre lists the sizes of the partials at 1, 2, ..., 8 times the base frequency, scaled to the same power.
  // They are the presets Pure, Mellow, Bright and Hollow of the mixer on page 2.
  var TIM = { pure: [1], mellow: [], bright: [], hollow: [] };
  for (var n = 1; n <= 8; n++) { TIM.mellow.push(1 / (n * n)); TIM.bright.push(1 / n); TIM.hollow.push(n % 2 ? 1 / n : 0); }
  var TPEAK = 0;
  Object.keys(TIM).forEach(function (k) {
    var a = TIM[k], s = 0; a.forEach(function (v) { s += v * v / 2; });
    TIM[k] = a.map(function (v) { return v / Math.sqrt(s); });
    var pk = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 4000; i++) { var th = 2 * Math.PI * i / 4000, y = 0; TIM[k].forEach(function (v, j) { y += v * Math.sin((j + 1) * th); }); pk = Math.max(pk, Math.abs(y)); }
    TPEAK = Math.max(TPEAK, pk);
  });
  var KN = PEAK / TPEAK, tim = "mellow";
  var ePitch = document.getElementById("nPitch"), eLoud = document.getElementById("nLoud"), eDur = document.getElementById("nDur");
  function f0() { return Math.round(110 * Math.pow(4, parseFloat(ePitch.value) / 1000)); }          // 110 to 440 Hz
  function dB() { return parseFloat(eLoud.value); }
  function dur() { return parseFloat(eDur.value) / 10; }                                           // 0.3 to 2 s
  function show() {
    var lv = dB();
    document.getElementById("nPitchO").textContent = f0() + " Hz";
    document.getElementById("nLoudO").textContent = (lv < 0 ? "−" + (-lv) : "0") + " dB";
    document.getElementById("nDurO").textContent = dur().toFixed(1) + " s";
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-tim]").forEach(function (b) { b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", b.getAttribute("data-tim") === tim ? "true" : "false"); });
  }
  function notePlay() {
    var f = f0(), g = KN * Math.pow(10, dB() / 20);
    play(synth(TIM[tim].map(function (v, j) { return { f: f * (j + 1), amp: g * v, tau: 0 }; }), dur(), 0.015, 0.03));
  }
  [ePitch, eLoud, eDur].forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener("input", show); el.addEventListener("change", notePlay); });
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-tim]").forEach(function (b) { b.addEventListener("click", function () { tim = b.getAttribute("data-tim"); show(); notePlay(); }); });
  document.getElementById("nPlay").addEventListener("click", notePlay);
  show();

  // ---- six instruments, one lowest frequency ----
  var F = 261.63, FT = 2.5;
  function steady(parts) { return parts.map(function (p) { return { f: p.f, amp: p.amp, tau: 0 }; }); }
  var INST = [
    { name: "Plucked string", make: function () { return synth(C.toHz(M.violin.partials({ pluck: 0.2 }), F), FT, 0.002, 0.05); } },
    { name: "Piano", make: function () { return synth(C.toHz(M.piano.partials({ f1: F, B: M.piano.B(60), rolloff: 9 }), F), FT, 0.002, 0.05); } },
    { name: "Clarinet", make: function () { return synth(steady(C.toHz(M.clarinet.partials(), F)), 1.6, 0.04, 0.08); } },
    { name: "Flute", make: function () { return flute(F, 1.6); } },
    { name: "Kalimba", make: function () { return synth(C.toHz(M.kalimba.partials({ f1: F }), F), FT, 0.002, 0.05); } },
    { name: "Drum", make: function () { return synth(C.toHz(drumParts(), F), FT, 0.002, 0.05); } }
  ];
  // Flute: harmonics with vibrato, plus breath noise. Harmonic levels (dB below the first) are typical of a
  // mezzo-forte note in the flute's low register, where the second harmonic is nearly as strong as the first
  // (J. Wolfe, J. Smith and colleagues, Flute acoustics, UNSW: https://newt.phys.unsw.edu.au/music/flute/).
  function flute(f, dur) {
    var N = Math.floor(dur * SR), d = new Float32Array(N), LV = [0, -4, -10, -16, -22, -28, -33, -38, -43, -48];
    var A = LV.map(function (v) { return Math.pow(10, v / 20); }), ph = 0, tone = new Float32Array(N), noise = new Float32Array(N);
    for (var n = 0; n < N; n++) {
      var t = n / SR, vd = 0.005 * Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (t - 0.25) / 0.3));          // vibrato fades in after 0.25 s
      ph += 2 * Math.PI * f * (1 + vd * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * 5.2 * t)) / SR;
      var y = 0;
      for (var k = 0; k < A.length; k++) { var on = Math.min(1, t / (0.05 + 0.012 * k)); y += A[k] * on * on * (3 - 2 * on) * Math.sin((k + 1) * ph); }
      tone[n] = y * (1 + 2 * vd * 10 * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * 5.2 * t + 0.6));         // the vibrato also swells the level a little
    }
    // breath: white noise through a band-pass filter near 2.5 kHz (RBJ biquad), louder at the start
    var w0 = 2 * Math.PI * 2500 / SR, al = Math.sin(w0) / (2 * 0.7), a0 = 1 + al, b0 = al / a0, b2 = -al / a0, a1 = -2 * Math.cos(w0) / a0, a2 = (1 - al) / a0;
    var x1 = 0, x2 = 0, y1 = 0, y2 = 0, seed = 12345;
    for (var m = 0; m < N; m++) {
      seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff; var x = seed / 0x3fffffff - 1;
      var yy = b0 * x + b2 * x2 - a1 * y1 - a2 * y2; x2 = x1; x1 = x; y2 = y1; y1 = yy; noise[m] = yy;
    }
    var rt = rmsOf(tone, 0.3, dur - 0.1), rn = rmsOf(noise, 0, dur), rel = Math.floor(0.08 * SR);
    for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      var t2 = i / SR, nl = 0.05 + 0.15 * Math.exp(-t2 / 0.05);                          // breath: 5% of the tone, more at the onset
      var e = Math.min(1, t2 / 0.03) * (i > N - rel ? (N - i) / rel : 1);
      d[i] = e * (tone[i] + nl * rt / rn * noise[i]);
    }
    return d;
  }
  // The stick stays on the skin for about 1.5 ms (modelled as a half-sine push), too long to start the high modes strongly:
  // a push of that shape has spectrum |cos(pi f tc)| / |1 - (2 f tc)^2| (1 at f = 0).
  var TC = 0.0015;
  function stick(f) { var u = 2 * f * TC; return Math.abs(u - 1) < 1e-9 ? Math.PI / 4 : Math.abs(Math.cos(Math.PI * f * TC) / (1 - u * u)); }
  function drumParts() { return M.drum.partials({ r: 0.35 }).map(function (p) { return { ratio: p.ratio, amp: p.amp * stick(p.ratio * F), tau: p.tau }; }); }
  var built = false;
  function buildAll() {
    if (built) return;
    // the same average strength (RMS over the first half second), then one common factor so the loudest peak is PEAK
    INST.forEach(function (it) { var d = it.make(), r = rmsOf(d, 0.02, 0.52); for (var i = 0; i < d.length; i++) d[i] /= r; it.data = d; });
    var pk = 0; INST.forEach(function (it) { pk = Math.max(pk, peakOf(it.data)); });
    INST.forEach(function (it) { var d = it.data; for (var i = 0; i < d.length; i++) d[i] *= PEAK / pk; });
    built = true;
  }
  var box = document.getElementById("fam");
  INST.forEach(function (it) {
    var b = document.createElement("button"); b.className = "primary"; b.textContent = "▶ " + it.name;
    b.addEventListener("click", function () { buildAll(); play(it.data); });
    box.appendChild(b);
  });
})();
</script>
```
